steps.title: Does the pinned-knight trick work?
steps.prompt: Predict first. In the second position Black has played the knight to f6 instead of g6. In the third, both sides have moved a rim pawn. Which change matters?

steps.text: **Before you grab or sacrifice.** Ask four things. How many pieces guard the target square, and how many attack it? Which pieces are pinned and cannot move or recapture? What would a check hit besides the king? What can the opponent's queen reach next move? [H] If you cannot answer all four, you are playing on hope.

steps.prompt: Teach it back. Imagine you teach a friend who knows how the pieces move. Write five sentences: (1) the conditions of the f7 sacrifice, (2) why the knight jump to g5 fails against the bishop on c5, (3) one position they could set up for the pinned-knight trick (name the pieces and squares, and which black knight must be missing), (4) one warning about a pawn you should not grab, (5) how to find out whether a trap works, using the four questions.

steps.text: **Self-check.** Did you name the conditions rather than the trap's name? Did you say what made the look-alike fail? Did you give a position a friend could set up on a board? Did you name a pawn or piece not to grab, and use the four questions (guards, pins, what a check hits, what the queen reaches)? Then go back to your first guess in the hook and rewrite it in one better sentence.

steps.prompt: Did your teach-back pass the self-check? Which of the five sentences was the weakest?

steps.text:
**What to remember.**
- A trap is a pattern with conditions: count guards, find pins, ask what a check hits.
- The f7 sacrifice needs a lone guard, a check with tempo and a second target.
- A pinned knight may jump if its threat is bigger than the queen.
- A free pawn is bait: ask what the queen can do next.
- Change one piece and the trick fails.
- [H] In three counted positions masters differed from the online crowd; a hint, not a rule.

steps.prompt: Go back to your very first answer in the hook. Rewrite it in a better sentence: your move for White and the conditions that make it work.
